357237.title: Chakraborti–Chen localized cycle-weight conjecture
357237.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices with $m$ edges, let $\K(G)$ denote its collection of cliques, and for each $T\in\K(G)$ let

$$
\gamma_G(T)=\max\{k:T\subseteq V(S)\text{ for some }S\subseteq G\text{ such that }S\cong C_k\}.
$$

For $t\geq 2$, define

$$
c'_G(T)=\frac{\binom{\gamma_G(T)}{2}}{\binom{\gamma_G(T)}{t}}.
$$

**Chakraborti–Chen localized cycle-weight conjecture.** The quantity $c'_G(T)$ is well-defined and decreasing in $\gamma_G(T)$, and

$$
\sum_{T\in\K(G)}c'_G(T)\leq m,
$$

with equality if and only if each $2$-connected component of $G$ is a complete graph of order at least $t$, together with any number of isolated vertices.
This conjecture is motivated by results of Chakraborti and Chen on bounded-circumference extremal problems; the supplied text gives no resolution.

357760.title: Strong arboricity versus arboricity conjecture
357760.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. Write $\operatorname{arb}(G)$ for its arboricity, the least number of colors in an edge coloring with no monochromatic cycle, and write $\zeta(G)$ for its strong arboricity, the least number of colors in a coloring that remains acyclic after contracting any single edge.

**Strong arboricity conjecture.** Every graph $G$ satisfies

$$
\zeta(G)\leqslant 2\operatorname{arb}(G).
$$

For complete graphs, the paper notes that $\zeta(K_n)=2\operatorname{arb}(K_n)-1$, motivating this proposed general upper bound.

358202.title: Tomon’s strong stability conjecture for 3-wise $t$-intersecting families
358202.statement:
Let $t\geq2$, let $0<p<p_0(t)$, and let $\mathcal G\subset 2^{[n]}$ be a **3-wise $t$-intersecting family**, meaning that the intersection of any three members has size at least $t$. Define

$$
p_0(t)=\frac{2}{\sqrt{4t+9}-1}
$$

and

$$
\mathcal F_0^t=\{F\subset[n]:|F\cap[t]|\geq t\}.
$$

**Tomon’s strong stability conjecture.** There exists $\epsilon=\epsilon(p,t)>0$ such that, if

$$
\mu_p(\mathcal G)>p^t-\epsilon,
$$

then $\mathcal G\subset\mathcal F$ for some $\mathcal F\cong\mathcal F_0^t$.

The conjecture strengthens the shifted-family stability result discussed in the paper by asserting containment in a canonical extremal family without a shifting hypothesis.

358412.title: Well-balanced orientation conjecture for maximum total arc-connectivity
358412.statement: Let $G$ be a graph, let $\vec{G}$ be an orientation of $G$, and let $tac(\vec{G})$ denote its total arc-connectivity. An orientation **maximizes total arc-connectivity** when it maximizes $tac(\vec{G})$ among all orientations of $G$. **Well-balanced orientation conjecture.** Every graph $G$ has an orientation $\vec{G}$ that maximizes $tac(\vec{G})$ and is well-balanced. The source presents this as a stronger statement than the conjecture about 2-edge-connected graphs and does not give a resolution.

358641.title: The zero forcing conjecture for Johnson graphs
358641.statement:
Let $G_n=K(n,2)$ be the Johnson graph whose vertices are the $2$-subsets of an $n$-element set, with two vertices adjacent when the corresponding subsets intersect in one element. For an integer $q\geq 0$, let $Z_q(G_n)$ denote the $q$-zero forcing number of $G_n$. **The zero forcing conjecture for $G_n$.** For any $n\geq 8$,

$$
Z_0(G_n)=\binom{n-1}{2}.
$$

Moreover,

$$
Z_0(G_n)=\binom{n}{2}-6\quad\text{for }n\in\{5,6,7\},
$$

and

$$
Z_0(G_n)=Z_1(G_n)\quad\text{for any }n\geq 7,
$$

while

$$
Z_1(G_n)=Z_0(G_n)+1\quad\text{for }n\in\{5,6\}.
$$

These claims refine the preceding exact values and bounds for the zero forcing numbers of the Johnson graphs $K(n,2)$; the source does not report a resolution.

359423.title: Crew's generalized degree sequence conjecture for trees
359423.statement:
Let $T$ be a tree. For a vertex subset $W\subseteq V(T)$, write $e(W)=|E(T[W])|$ and let $d(W)$ be the number of edges of $T$ with exactly one endpoint in $W$. The **generalized degree sequence** of $T$ is the multiset

$$
\{(|W|,e(W),d(W)): W\subseteq V(T)\}.
$$

**Crew's conjecture.** For any tree $T$, the generalized degree sequence of $T$ is determined by $X_T$.

This extends the fact that restricting to singleton subsets recovers the ordinary degree sequence. The source presents it as an interesting problem posed by Crew; its resolution is not indicated, so it remains open.

360121.title: Equitable 2-colourability conjecture for even cycle decompositions
360121.statement:
Let $v\geq \ell\geq 4$ be even integers, and let $I$ be a 1-factor of $K_v$. An **equitably 2-colourable** $\ell$-cycle decomposition of $K_v-I$ is an $\ell$-cycle decomposition whose vertices admit a red-blue colouring with colour classes differing in size by at most one on each cycle. The divisibility condition is that $\ell$ divides the number of edges of $K_v-I$:

$$
\ell\mid \frac{v(v-2)}{2}.
$$

**Even-cycle equitable-colourability conjecture.** There exists an equitably 2-colourable $\ell$-cycle decomposition of $K_v-I$ if and only if

$$
\ell\mid \frac{v(v-2)}{2}.
$$

The paper leaves the more general existence question for equitably 2-colourable odd cycle decompositions of the cocktail party graph open; the stated even-order conjecture is likewise presented as unresolved.

360570.title: Anti-van der Waerden conjecture for products with peripheral trees
360570.statement:
Let $T$ be a $k$-peripheral tree and let $G$ be a nontrivial connected graph. The anti-van der Waerden number $\operatorname{aw}(T\square G,k)$ is the least number of colors in a rainbow-free exact $k$-coloring of $T\square G$.

**Peripheral-tree product conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{aw}(T\square G,k)=k.
$$

This conjecture proposes that the anti-van der Waerden number of the Cartesian product of any nontrivial connected graph with a $k$-peripheral tree is exactly $k$. It generalizes the preceding result for $3$-peripheral trees, but the surrounding examples indicate that peripheral structure alone may not fully characterize all tree products.

363418.title: Conjecture on perfect spanning sets in finite abelian groups
363418.statement: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group, let $A\subseteq G$ be an $m$-subset, and call $A$ a **perfect $s$-spanning set** when every element of $G$ arises as a signed sum of at most $s$ terms in a unique way. **Perfect spanning set conjecture.** If $A$ is a perfect $s$-spanning set, then one of the following holds: $m=1$, $G\cong\mathbb{Z}_{2s+1}$, and $A=\{a\}$ for some $a\in\mathbb{Z}_{2s+1}$ with $\gcd(a,2s+1)=1$; $s=1$, and $G$ is the disjoint union of $\{0\}$, $A$, and $-A$; or $m=2$, $G\cong\mathbb{Z}_{2s^2+2s+1}$, and $A=d\cdot\{s,s+1\}$ for some $d\in\mathbb{Z}_{2s+1}$ with $\gcd(d,2s^2+2s+1)=1$. Perfect spanning sets are known in the cases $m=1$, $s=1$, and $m=2$; the conjecture asserts that there are no others.

364089.title: The toroidal 5-choosability and 5-colorability conjecture
364089.statement:
A graph drawn on the torus is a **toroidal graph**, and it is **5-choosable** if every assignment of lists of at least five colors to its vertices admits a proper coloring from those lists. It is **5-colorable** if it admits a proper coloring with five colors.

**The toroidal 5-choosability conjecture.** A toroidal graph is $5$-choosable if and only if it is $5$-colorable.

The paper establishes this equivalence under additional structural assumptions, while the unrestricted statement remains open.

364453.title: Invariant graph conjecture for marked rational maps
364453.statement:
Let $(f,P)$ be a marked rational map, with Julia set $J_f$, and let $G$ be a graph in the sphere. An **$f$-invariant graph** satisfies $f(G)=G$; the post-critical set is denoted by $P$. **Invariant graph conjecture.** Theorem should hold with $n=1$: there exists an $f$-invariant graph

$$
G\subset J_f
$$

such that

$$
P\cap J_f\subset G
$$

and each component of

$$
\overline{\mathbb C}\setminus G
$$

contains at most one point of $P$. The conjecture would follow in particular from the corresponding invariant-graph statement for marked expanding Thurston maps; the paper explains that it is known under certain Julia-set hypotheses, but leaves the general case open.

364679.title: Adiprasito–Schmidt stability conjecture for partition rank
364679.statement:
Let $d\geq 2$, let $q$ be a prime power, and let $T\in\mathbb{F}_q^{n_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes\mathbb{F}_q^{n_d}$. Write $\overline{\mathbb{F}}_q$ for an algebraic closure of $\mathbb{F}_q$ and $T^{\overline{\mathbb{F}}_q}$ for the scalar extension of $T$. **Stability conjecture for partition rank.** There exists a constant $C\coloneqq C(d,q)>0$ such that

$$
\operatorname{PR}_{\mathbb{F}_q}(T)\leq C\operatorname{PR}_{\overline{\mathbb{F}}_q}\left(T^{\overline{\mathbb{F}}_q}\right).
$$

The source recalls this as an open stability conjecture; it also explains that the three rank conjectures recalled there are proved equivalent later in the paper.

365135.title: The additive reachability conjecture
365135.statement: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be the stable category of the Frobenius category $\mathcal{F}$, let $T$ be a cluster-tilting object, let $\Sigma$ denote the suspension, and let $\mathcal{E}(\mathcal{C})$ be the exchange graph of cluster-tilting objects. **Additive reachability conjecture.** If there is a path in $\mathcal{E}(\mathcal{C})$ connecting $T$ and $\Sigma T$, then $\mathcal{E}(\mathcal{C})$ has exactly one connected component. This is the additive form of reachability: the stated hypothesis is equivalent to injective reachability, while the conjectured connectedness of the exchange graph remains unresolved in general.

365359.title: Graham–Häggkvist conjecture for complete bipartite hosts
365359.statement:
A graph **decomposes** $G$ if copies of the graph form a perfect packing of $G$, and $K_{n,n}$ denotes the complete bipartite graph with $n$ vertices in each part.

**Graham–Häggkvist complete-bipartite conjecture.** Any tree of order $n+1$ decomposes the complete bipartite graph $K_{n,n}$.

This follows from the stated conjecture that every tree of order $n+1$ decomposes every $n$-regular bipartite graph. The source reports approximate results and evidence, but the exact assertion remains open.

365453.title: The local antimagic chromatic number conjecture for joins of matching and null graphs
365453.statement:
Let $r,s\ge 1$ and $m\ge 2$. For a graph $G$, its **local antimagic chromatic number** $\chi_{la}(G)$ is the least number of distinct induced vertex labels among bijective local antimagic edge labelings of $G$. Let $(2s+1)P_2$ be the disjoint union of $2s+1$ copies of the two-vertex path, let $O_m$ be the null graph on $m$ vertices, let $\vee$ denote the graph join, and let $2r((2s+1)P_2\vee O_m)$ be the disjoint union of $2r$ copies of this join.

**Local antimagic chromatic number conjecture.**

$$
\chi_{la}\bigl(2r((2s+1)P_2\vee O_m)\bigr)=3.
$$

This is posed as an open problem in the conclusion, extending results on local antimagic chromatic numbers for joins of special graph families. The claim predicts a constant value of $3$ throughout the stated parameter range.

365534.title: Qiao, Park and Koolen's bounded-diameter conjecture for amply regular graphs
365534.statement: Let $G$ be a connected amply regular graph with parameters $(n,d,\alpha,\beta)$, and let $0<\varepsilon<1$ be a real number. **Qiao, Park and Koolen's conjecture.** There exists a constant $K(\varepsilon)$ such that, if $\beta>\varepsilon d\geq 1$ and $\beta\geq\alpha$, then the diameter of $G$ is at most $K(\varepsilon)$. The conjecture is motivated by the known bound $\operatorname{diam}(G)\leq 7$ when $\beta>d/3\geq 1$ and $\beta\geq\alpha$; whether a bound depending only on $\varepsilon$ holds in the stated generality remains open.

365651.title: The generalized Berge–Fulkerson conjecture for r-graphs
365651.statement: Let $r\geq 1$. An **$r$-graph** is the graph class defined in the source, and a **perfect matching** is a set of edges meeting every vertex exactly once. **The generalized Berge–Fulkerson conjecture.** Every $r$-graph has $2r$ perfect matchings such that every edge is in precisely two of them. This generalizes the Berge–Fulkerson phenomenon for cubic graphs; the supplied text gives no resolution status.

365685.title: The partition conjecture for k-clique isolating sets
365685.statement: Let $k \geq 3$ be an integer. A **$k$-clique isolating set** of a graph is a vertex set whose closed neighborhood leaves no copy of $K_k$. **The partition conjecture.** Every connected graph, except $K_k$, can be partitioned into $k+1$ disjoint $k$-clique isolating sets. This would imply the known upper bound $\iota(G,k) \leq n/(k+1)$ for connected graphs $G \ncong K_k$, and the paper studies this conjecture without resolving it.

365891.title: Generalized truncated Jacobi triple product conjecture
365891.statement:
Let $R$ and $S$ be positive integers with $1\leq S<R$, let $k>\ell\geq1$, and assume $k\geq4$. There exists an integer $N$ such that the theta series

$$
\frac{(-1)^{k-1}\left(\sum_{j=-k+1}^{k}-\sum_{j=-\ell+1}^{\ell}\right)(-1)^j q^{Rj(j+1)/2+Sj}}{(q^S,q^{R-S},q^R;q^R)_\infty}
$$

has nonnegative coefficients for $n\geq N$.
**Generalized truncated Jacobi triple product conjecture.** Under these conditions, the asserted eventual coefficientwise nonnegativity holds.
This is proposed as a generalized truncated version of the Andrews–Merca–Guo–Zeng conjecture. The paper also gives an equivalent formulation in terms of the partition function $P_{R,S}(n)$, but does not prove the conjecture.

366137.title: Cutset finiteness conjecture for graphs of dimension greater than one
366137.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, and let $\operatorname{Dim}(G)$ denote its dimension parameter. **Cutset finiteness conjecture.** Every graph satisfying

$$
\operatorname{Dim}(G)>1
$$

has

$$
\kappa<\infty.
$$

The conjecture proposes that finiteness of the cutset-growth parameter is exactly the geometric criterion corresponding to $p_c<1$. The source explicitly states that this remains an important open problem; in particular, it is not resolved by the paper's results.
